notes.text: Dylan Larkin is suspended and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-six forward.
Jacob Bernard-Docker has not dressed for the last 15 games.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Conor Geekie takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside McDonagh and Crozier.
Anthony Cirelli is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. Nikita Kucherov has taken his spot beside Jake Guentzel and Brandon Hagel.
Brayden Point is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Brandon Hagel has taken his spot beside Nikita Kucherov and Jake Guentzel.
Erik Černák is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. Max Crozier has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.
Gage Goncalves returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Sam O'Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Yanni Gourde and Jake Guentzel.

story.head: The Red Wings are searching for answers
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Tampa Bay on Nov 3. The Lightning have won two in a row, while the Red Wings are on a five-game losing streak. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Wings last (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Lightning first (tied for fifth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.425) says: their chances are worth about .562, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.669), largely thanks to their finishing.
In their five-game skid, the Red Wings have been outscored 18-9, including 13-7 at 5-on-5.

The Red Wings leave the shooting to their forwards (4th lowest) and ice the puck a lot (30th). The Lightning, by contrast, rarely ice the puck (4th). The Red Wings also block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), so the Red Wings are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Lightning’s shots. On the other side, the Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), but don't block many shots (29th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.89 goals a game, the fourth most in the league.

Lucas Raymond (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 20 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Nikita Kucherov (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 19 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (13 G / 11 A / 24 P in 19 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (9-4-1 / .884 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay. Detroit has two options in net: John Gibson (4-7-1 / .862 SV% in 13 GS) and Daniil Tarasov (2-3-2 / .919 SV% in 6 GS). Gibson has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday, so Detroit could turn to Tarasov to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrincat, Finnie and Kasper. One more thing: the Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Red Wings do.
